We want to know: after any sequence of such operations (including possibly none), what is the smallest value that must appear in every possible final array? And we return that smallest unavoidable element.

Another way: Among all possible final arrays reachable via these operations, consider the set of elements that appear in every such final array. We want the minimum element of that set.

We need to derive a characterization of reachable final arrays. This problem appears similar to known Codeforces/LeetCode problems: "Maximum Array Value" (the given function name) is known problem: you can merge adjacent elements if left <= right (or left >= right) and you want the maximum possible final element. In fact, there is a known LeetCode problem 2443: "Maximum Array Value", where you can merge if nums[i] <= nums[i+1] and you replace nums[i+1] with sum and delete nums[i]; you want to maximize the last element. The solution is to traverse from right to left, maintaining a running sum, and whenever current element <= sum, you can merge it into sum; else you start a new segment. The answer is the maximum segment sum.

But here the condition is reversed: we can merge if left >= right. And the question is different: we want the smallest unavoidable element in the final array.

Thus we can only merge a left element into its right neighbor if it is not smaller than the right neighbor.
